sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 19 › Telecom technologies - 3G to 5G and 6G roadmap, satellite communication, optical fibre › Optical fibre - working principle, signal form, undersea cables (CANI), national fibre targets
bullets: Works on total internal reflection; signals travel as pulses of light (LENS Sep 2025). It is the fastest data-transmission medium compared with copper cable, radio waves and satellite signals (APPSC 2025 asked).
Main use is communication; single-mode fibre carries signals over long distances, multi-mode over short runs .

Undersea cables are fibre-optic lines on the seabed, about 1.5 million km globally; optical repeaters every 60-80 km; carry nearly 99% of international internet and telecom traffic; cheaper and lower-latency than satellites (LENS Sep 2025).

National fibre: NOFN planned to link all 2,50,000 Gram Panchayats using existing PSU fibre (BSNL, RailTel, Power Grid); funded by USOF; uses GPON technology; est. cost Rs 20,000 cr (APP). NOFN was later renamed BharatNet .
Exam angle: statement sets on TIR, light signals and single-mode fibre ("All of the above").

bullets: Router: Role Connects different networks, routes by IP; OSI layer Network (3)
Modem: Role Modulator-demodulator: digital <→ analog; OSI layer Physical
Transmission modes: simplex (one way: radio/TV broadcast, keyboard), half duplex (both ways, one at a time: walkie-talkie), full duplex (both at once: telephone) .

Connections: DSL runs on the telephone copper line, cable on coaxial TV cable, fibre on light pulses in optical fibre . Satellite internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and needs no terrestrial wire.

Arid/desert: Formation / parent material Wind-laid sand, low rainfall; Key traits Sandy, saline, low humus and N; kankar lower down; Main regions W Rajasthan

Black (regur / black cotton): Area / share 5.47 lakh sq km, 16.6%; Origin and properties From basalt (Deccan Trap); clay >62%; high moisture retention; deep cracks, "self-ploughing"; neutral to alkaline; rich in Ca, K, Mg, poor in N, P, humus; Where Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, W. AP, N. Karnataka; Crops Cotton, jowar, chillies, tobacco

Red and yellow: Area / share 5.18 lakh sq km; Origin and properties Red from iron oxide; porous, light; poor in lime, humus, phosphoric acid; low moisture retention; Where Kanyakumari-Jhansi, Kutch-Rajmahal; Crops Ragi, groundnut, tobacco

Peaty soils form where heavy rainfall and high humidity keep soil waterlogged and organic matter piles up (APP). (The OCR answer key of the APPSC-G1 2024 peaty-soil question reads "semi-arid climate with salinity", which describes saline soils. Follow the waterlogged-organic description.)

bullets: State average rainfall ~966 mm; Rayalaseema and south coast depend more on the NE monsoon.
Retreating monsoon: withdraws October-November; Bay of Bengal cyclones bring the rain of this season to the southern states.
SW monsoon (June-September) gives ~2/3 (65-70%) of AP's rainfall. It sets in during the 2nd week of June; July is the wettest month (CDI; APP).
Normal rainfall (APSES 2024-25): SWM 574.7 mm + NEM 285.3 mm = ~860 mm a year. CDI prints a State average of ~966 mm (older figure). 2024: SWM 681.6 mm (+18.6%); NEM 278.7 mm (-2.3%).

The IMD report *Observed Rainfall Variability and Changes over Andhra Pradesh State* ranks the south-western region (Rayalaseema) lowest in annual rainfall (APPSC-GS 2023). It describes AP's climate as generally hot and humid, with summer from March to June (APPSC-GS 2025).

Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Samithis and Zilla Parishads Act, 1959 : Panchayat Samithi at the block and Zilla Parishad at the district, over village panchayats. It gave effect to AP's 3-tier system of 1 Nov 1959 (CDX).

Andhra Pradesh: the NTR government replaced Panchayat Samithis with Mandal Praja Parishads (Mandal Praja Parishads Act, 1986) . This was a mandal-level tier in the Ashok Mehta mould. AP still runs Mandal Praja Parishads and Zilla Praja Parishads (TH, 8 Sep 2026).

The Government appoints the Governor, Deputy Governors and Board, and can supersede the Board (Sec 30) . The MPC and inflation-targeting law (2016) gave RBI operational independence on rates.

Spillover channels: capital outflows, rupee pressure and imported inflation. RBI's special FCNR(B) and forex measures drew about $32 bn after the June policy (TH, 27 Jul 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Inflation - types, causes, measurement (CPI, WPI, core inflation), effects and control measures › Phillips curve - inflation-unemployment trade-off
bullets: Phillips curve: inverse relation between inflation and unemployment - lower unemployment comes with higher inflation .

India's curve is flat: IIP-CPI data (2012-2026) show little trade-off; ~92% of workers are informal with no wage-bargaining power, so wages do not rise with output (TH, 7 Sep 2026; LENSD, 8 Sep 2026).

bullets: Income originating: value produced within the State's boundaries (this is GSDP). Income accruing = State income + income of the State's residents earned in other States/abroad.

GSDP is computed across 9 sectors (APPSC-G2 2017). These are the old CSO classification: agriculture-forestry-fishing; mining; manufacturing; electricity-gas-water; construction; trade-hotels; transport-storage-communication; finance-real estate; community and social services .
GVA (basic prices, industry-wise) + product taxes - product subsidies = GSDP (market prices). NSDP = GSDP - depreciation, and AP's per capita income is based on NSDP.
Directorate of Economics & Statistics (DES), AP compiles GSDP; at State level the DESs compile State Domestic Product; for GSDP the economy is divided into 9 sectors (G2 2017).

Entanglement sudden death = abrupt total loss of entanglement; Raman Research Institute showed one well-timed local "quantum flip" can delay or prevent it (LENS daily, 16 Sep 2026).

Supremacy machines: Google Sycamore (2019) ; China's photonic Jiuzhang (2020) . Micius (China, 2016) = first quantum communication satellite . Microsoft's Majorana 2 chip raised qubit stability to 20-60 s (APPCA, 2026).

100% stamp duty and registration fee exemption for tech firms in the Valley (APPCA, Jun 2026); plan to train 4.5 million people in AI and quantum.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › International trade - composition and direction of India's exports and imports; trade deficit › Direction of trade - destinations, sources, largest partner
bullets: Source: IYB 2026. From these shares, India runs a surplus with the USA and Netherlands and a deficit with China, Russia, UAE, Saudi Arabia (oil and goods imports exceed exports).

China became India's largest trading partner in FY 2025-26, overtaking the USA: trade $151.1 bn; goods deficit with China over $100 bn (APPCA Jun 2026). Calendar 2025 (Chinese data): trade $155.62 bn, deficit $116.12 bn; H1 2026 imports from China a record $79.41 bn (TH, 15 Jul 2026).
Imports from China: APIs, solar PV cells, semiconductor chips, telecom machinery; exports to China: iron ore, cotton, chemicals, marine products (APPCA).
BRICS: trade $417.5 bn in FY26; deficit with BRICS $226.1 bn; imports from China $131.6 bn; UAE is the largest BRICS export market ($37.4 bn) (LENSD, 10 Sep 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Fiscal policy - objectives, instruments; fiscal, revenue, primary and effective revenue deficits › Subsidies - heads, fertiliser, DBT, hidden subsidies
bullets: Major subsidy heads: food, fertiliser, petroleum (LPG) . Subsidies can be explicit (food, fertiliser, export and interest subsidies) or implicit/hidden (under-pricing of education, health and other public services; tax concessions and cheap credit) (APP; for tax concessions).
Urea is the largest fertiliser subsidy item .
DBT in fertiliser (national rollout 2018): the subsidy goes to companies after retail sale is recorded on PoS machines with Aadhaar authentication of the buyer .

Current: major subsidies rose 37.4% in Q1 FY27 because of a spike in crude oil (West Asia); they may overshoot the budget by about ₹50,000 crore (TH, 21 Aug 2026). The 16th FC asks for subsidy rationalisation.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Public expenditure - revenue and capital, developmental and non-developmental, trends; subsidies › Subsidies - major heads, explicit vs hidden, NBS, Oil Pool Account
bullets: Budget 2026-27: total subsidies ₹4,54,773 crore (-3.1% vs 2025-26 RE); food ₹2,27,629 crore and fertiliser ₹1,70,799 crore = 87% of the bill; LPG ₹12,085 crore (CDI Budget analysis). Major subsidies (food, fertiliser, petroleum) ₹4.11 lakh crore = 1.0% of GDP.

sections.topic: Money supply · High-powered money (M0 / reserve money)
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-4 › Money supply - M0 to M4, high-powered money, money multiplier, velocity › High-powered money (M0 / reserve money) - components
bullets: Also called reserve money, monetary base, base money, central bank money; basis of credit creation; the most important money indicator for RBI.
As the PYQ frames it: H = currency held by the public + cash reserves of commercial banks (with themselves and with RBI) + other deposits with RBI.
'Other' deposits with RBI: quasi-government and financial institutions (incl. primary dealers), foreign central banks and governments, international agencies such as the IMF.
Uses (components) side: currency held by the public + cash reserves of banks (cash in hand + deposits with RBI) + other deposits with RBI (this is the APPSC-G2 2025 answer).
Money multiplier = M3 / M0. A higher CRR, a higher SLR or a higher currency-deposit ratio (cdr) lowers it. A stronger banking habit raises it (UPSC 2019).

sections.topic: Supreme Court and High Court Judges
sections.where: Rocket Sheets · Indian Polity › #71 · Supreme Court and High Court Judges
bullets: Supreme Court Judges are governed under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution.
The Governor has no power to appoint High Court Judges.
A distinguished jurist is eligible for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge under Article 124(3)(c).
The President transfers High Court Judges on the advice of a collegium led by the Chief Justice of India.
Another Judge of the same High Court may exercise writ jurisdiction over the High Court Chief Justice’s administrative actions.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › High Courts and subordinate judiciary; judicial review, judicial activism, PIL and judicial overreach debate › High Court judges - appointment, transfer, resignation, removal instances, writ and supervisory powers, contempt
bullets: Under Art. 217, the President appoints after consulting the CJI and the Governor, and for puisne judges also the HC Chief Justice. Proposals start with the HC Chief Justice and the HC collegium (CJ + 2), then go to the SC collegium (CJI + 2 senior-most judges) (LENSD 12 Aug 2026).
The inquiry report on Yashwant Varma (formerly Allahabad HC) was to be tabled despite his resignation (LENSD 11 Jul 2026).

Contempt: Arts. 129 and 215 make the SC and HCs courts of record. The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 followed the H.N. Sanyal Committee and defines civil contempt (wilful disobedience) and criminal contempt (scandalising or obstructing justice). Fair criticism and accurate reporting are exceptions (VIS 2026).
Art. 215: every HC is a court of record; punishes contempt of itself and subordinate courts (SC: Art. 129).

Appellate: primarily a court of appeal; second civil appeals on questions of law only; death sentences of Sessions Courts need HC confirmation (now under BNSS 2023, which replaced CrPC from 1 July 2024) .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-2 › Governor - appointment, powers, discretionary powers, position and controversies (Article 200/201, Article 356 reports) › Appointment and office - Articles 153-158, same Governor for two states, qualifications, pleasure (B.P. Singhal)
bullets: Art. 155: appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal. The Governor is neither directly nor indirectly elected.

The term is 5 years, but he continues until his successor enters office . So "quits office immediately after the term expires" is the wrong statement (APPSC-G1 2019). He resigns to the President, may be transferred, and may be reappointed.

In B.P. Singhal v. UoI (2010), the pleasure doctrine is not unfettered: a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or merely because the Centre's government changes, and removal is open to limited judicial review . No grounds for removal are stated in the Constitution.
Grounds for removal are not stated in the Constitution. The President may transfer a Governor, and a Governor may be reappointed (APP).

Art 200 reservation: mandatory for bills endangering the High Court's position (APP; IYB). The President has an absolute veto over reserved bills (APP). APPSC 2025 key: reservation is an example of central control over states.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-1 › Structural change - sectoral composition of output and employment; the missing manufacturing transition › Clark-Fisher / Lewis model of structural transformation
bullets: Three-sector (Clark-Fisher): Author Allan Fisher and Colin Clark; Prediction As income rises, labour and output shift primary → secondary → tertiary

Dual-sector: Author W. Arthur Lewis (1954); Prediction Surplus farm labour (marginal productivity ~zero) moves to the modern industrial sector at a constant wage until the surplus is exhausted - the Lewis turning point
India deviates: output shifted to services while labour stayed on farms, so the Lewis transfer is slow (~46% of workers still in agriculture).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-2 › Trends in India's national income, per capita income and sectoral shares; inter-state GSDP comparison › Sectoral share of GVA - at Independence vs now
bullets: At Independence agriculture was the largest contributor to GDP (APPSC 2023). Industry was about 13% of GDP in 1950-51 (APPSC 2023 key).
Agriculture's share had fallen to about 17% by 2017-18 (APPSC 2019). Services now make up over 50% of GDP, so the order is services > industry > agriculture.
Sector growth, FY 2025-26: agriculture 3.1% (4.6% the year before), industry 6.2%, manufacturing 7.0%, services 9.1% (ES 2025-26; LENS, Jan 2026).
The 2022-23 series raised agriculture's GVA by 3.8-5.9% and cut trade by 36% (TH, 16 Sep 2026).

bullets: GDP deflator = Nominal GDP (current prices) / Real GDP (constant prices) x 100 (APPSC-G2 2025).
It is the most comprehensive price measure because it covers all goods and services in GDP (consumption, investment, government, exports), not a fixed basket like CPI/WPI .
GDP deflator = GDP at current prices / GDP at constant prices x 100 - the most comprehensive measure of inflation (covers all final goods and services, not a fixed basket) (G2 2025 key).

bullets: Art. 178: the Speaker is elected from among the members.
Vacating office (Art. 179): he ceases to be a member, resigns to the Deputy Speaker, or is removed by a resolution of a majority of all the then members, with 14 days' notice.
The Deputy Speaker (Art. 178) acts with full powers when the Speaker's post is vacant or he is absent. The Chairman of the Council resigns to the Deputy Chairman.
Elected by the Assembly (Art. 178). The Speaker holds office for the life of the Assembly (APP) and continues after dissolution until the new Assembly first meets .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 22 › Biodiversity hotspots in India; endemism; Biological Diversity Act 2002 and access-benefit sharing › Access and benefit sharing - benefit-sharing cases (Kani tribe, Arogyapacha)
bullets: ABS means commercial benefits from bioresources are shared with the communities that provide them. It covers plant, animal and microbial resources and traditional knowledge, but excludes human genetic material. The CBD introduced it in 1992 and the Nagoya Protocol put it into operation in 2010.

Kani model : the Kani tribe of Kerala shared knowledge of Arogyapacha (Trichopus zeylanicus). TBGRI, Thiruvananthapuram, used it to develop the anti-fatigue drug "Jeevani" and shared the licence fee and royalty with a Kani trust. It was the first well-known benefit-sharing model.
NBA's ABS has raised over ₹266 crore since 2008. Red Sanders accounts for 45% (₹120 crore) of that and the seed sector for 32.3% (LENSD, 26 Jun 2026).

New fund rules (NBA): if a resource comes from an identifiable repository, 25-40% of ABS funds go to it and 60-75% go to local communities through SBBs/UTBCs. If the origin cannot be traced, the money goes to conservation (VIS Apr 2026). India also notified ABS Regulations 2025, which cover Digital Sequence Information (APPCA).

APSBB plans a first-of-its-kind Marine ABS framework for fishermen and will strengthen about 13,000 BMCs (TH, 30 Apr 2026). NBA sanctioned ₹82 lakh to APSBB for Red Sanders conservation (LENS Oct 2025).

sections.topic: Election Commission of India · Disputes regarding election
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Election Commission of India - composition, appointment (2023 Act), powers and functions › Disputes regarding election - EC vs courts, Article 329 bar
bullets: Art. 329(a): laws on delimitation and allotment of seats cannot be questioned in court; Art. 329(b): an election can be challenged only by an election petition .

By convention courts do not interfere once the poll process begins; the ECI cannot review a result. Petitions go to the High Court (Parliament, state legislatures) and the Supreme Court for President/VP (Art. 71) (UPSC).

Art. 329(b): an election to Parliament or a state legislature can be questioned only by an election petition under the RPA 1951. Such petitions are tried by the High Court, with appeal to the Supreme Court .
President/VP election disputes: decided by the Supreme Court (Art. 71) .
The ECI does not try election petitions. It decides party and symbol disputes and advises on disqualification.

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Recognition of national and state parties - criteria and the Symbols Order › Election Symbols Order 1968 - reserved vs free symbols, split disputes (Sadiq Ali)
bullets: Reserved symbols: exclusively for recognised parties (e.g. Lotus - BJP, Hand - INC); two recognised parties in different States may hold the same symbol.
Free symbols: for RUPPs and independents, allotted from a notified list; latest list May 2025 - 184 symbols (LENSD, 11 Jun 2026).
RUPPs get a common symbol if they contest 2 Lok Sabha seats or 5% of Assembly seats (LENSD, 11 Sep 2026).

Split disputes: Para 15 - the ECI decides which faction is the party, applying the Sadiq Ali (1971) test of majority [GK for the test] (TH, 16 Jun 2026); the ECI acts as a court in recognition and symbol disputes.
Para 16A: the ECI may suspend or withdraw recognition for defying the Model Code of Conduct (TH, 5 May 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Elections - delimitation, model code of conduct, EVM-VVPAT, NOTA, election petitions › Election machinery - CEO, DEO, Returning Officer, observers
bullets: Chief Electoral Officer (CEO): Role Assists the ECI in each State/UT; verifies non-compliant RUPPs
District Election Officer (DEO): Role District level (usually the Collector) ; receives expense accounts within 30 days (Sec. 78)
Returning Officer: Role Conducts the poll in a constituency, declares results
Observers: Role General, police and expenditure observers appointed by the ECI (Sec. 20B)
During elections the ECI controls officers on poll duty - can transfer them or act against partisan conduct (APP).

bullets: Rayalaseema lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and the Karnataka/Telangana highlands, so it gets little SW-monsoon rain (CDI). Anantapur is the lowest-rainfall district.
Chronic droughts hit Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam when the NE monsoon fails; groundwater depletion adds to this (CDI).

2026: a deficient year. The SW monsoon deficit reached 51.2% (1 Jun-25 Aug), with all 28 districts deficient. Causes: El Nino subsidence, and all seven low-pressure systems forming at the head of the Bay (CDCA Aug 2026).

bullets: Current relevance: the 2026 El Niño drought has made the Irrigation Calendar a priority, with Veligonda Phase-I commissioned on 31 Aug 2026 (TH).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern › Universal angles
bullets: Current relevance: El Niño hit the 2026 kharif. AP had a 51% rainfall deficit from 1 June to 25 August, and all 28 districts were in deficit. 20.35 lakh ha was sown, against 25.63 lakh ha a year earlier (TH, 28 Aug 2026).
AP angle: the survey's list of constraints is fragmented holdings (below 1 ha), monsoon dependence, soil-fertility loss and weak credit (APSES; CDI).
Criticism & debates: heavy monsoon dependence. About 50% of net sown area is rainfed and 86% of holdings are under 2 ha (LENSD, 8 Jun 2026).
AP rainfall 51% below normal (India 13%) to 25 Aug; sown area 20.35 lakh ha vs 25.63 lakh ha last year, with a planned shift to pulses and drought-resilient crops (TH, 28 Aug 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-1 › Climate change - evidence, natural and anthropogenic causes, global warming, IPCC assessments, impacts › Impacts
bullets: Sea level: thermal expansion plus ice melt; uninhabited South Pacific islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea submerged in 1999; Kiribati, Tuvalu at risk (APP).

Coral bleaching: the 1.2 degC threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse is already crossed; beyond ~2 degC parts of the Amazon may turn savanna (UN brief, LENSD 24 Jun 2026). Reefs need 15+ years to recover (APP).
Oceans and species: acidity up 30% since the Industrial Revolution (CDI); up to 25% of mountain species face extinction (AR6, CDI).

Extremes and agriculture: India 2025 - 4,419 deaths and 17.4 million ha of crops damaged by extreme weather (WMO 2025, CDI); buffalo milk yields in Haryana's trans-Gangetic plains hit by warming (TH, 6 Jul 2026).
Disease spread: warmer, wetter conditions widen the range of vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue.

bullets: Three stages (Bhabha, 1954): (1) PHWRs run on natural uranium with a heavy-water moderator. (2) Fast breeder reactors burn the plutonium from stage 1 and breed more fuel than they consume. (3) Thorium reactors (AHWR). India's thorium reserves are the world's 3rd largest, about 3.6 lakh tonnes (CDI).
Capacity is 8.78 GW, about 3% of generation. It is expected to reach 22.38 GW by 2031-32. LENSD).
Uranium: Jaduguda and Narwapahar (Jharkhand), Tummalapalle (YSR Kadapa, AP); Indian ore is low-grade (APPCA 2026).

Thorium from monazite and ilmenite beach sands (Kerala, TN, AP, Odisha); fuel for the third stage of the three-stage programme and the AHWR. Thorium about 360,000 t (about 25% of world reserves), natural uranium about 70,000 t (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 5 Science, Tech & Environment › 21 › Coal sector - reserves, production, washing, commercial mining, coal gasification › Coal sector problems - ash, washing, rail evacuation, productivity
bullets: Indian coal has high ash (35-45%), a low calorific value, a high ash-fusion temperature and low sulphur (~0.5%) (APPCA, Jun 2026).
BPSC key: all four are problems: poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports, and administrative issues.
Rail and logistics delays often disrupt thermal power generation (CDI Block09). Coking coal is imported mainly from Australia; non-coking coal comes from Indonesia and South Africa (APPCA).

sections.topic: Industrial policy · Foreign investment and technology agreements
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-3 › Industrial policy - resolutions of 1948, 1956, 1977, 1980 and the New Industrial Policy 1991 › Foreign investment and technology agreements - automatic approval, 51% limit
bullets: New Industrial Policy announced 24 July 1991.

Automatic approval for up to 51% foreign equity in a list of high-priority, high-investment, high-technology industries (e.g. capital goods, entertainment electronics, food processing) - not all industries (APPSC-G1 2012); also for export trading companies.
Automatic approval for foreign technology agreements in high-priority industries; use of foreign brand names/trademarks permitted; Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) set up to speed approvals.
Mandatory convertibility clause (lenders converting loans to equity) was relaxed for term loans; APPSC-G2 2025 key: it applies only to term loans of less than 10 years - learn the key's wording.

Now: FDI up to 100% under the automatic route in most sectors, negative-list approach; FIPB abolished June 2017; approvals via FIF portal, integrated with National Single Window System since Aug 2022 (IYB 2026).

sections.topic: Single Desk Portal and the Single Window Clearance Act
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Approaches and initiatives in AP industry - industrial policy, single desk, MSMEs, industrial nodes › Single Desk Portal and the Single Window Clearance Act - timelines, deemed approval
bullets: The statute is the AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002; 2015 is the launch year of the Single Desk Portal (April 2015). The Act was amended by the AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026, passed Aug 2026 (TH, 20 Aug 2026).

The SDP gives end-to-end processing of 93+ clearances across 19 departments within 21 days. Approvals fall into three categories: self-certification; in-principle approval then inspection; deemed approval if the SLA is breached.
It gives pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals within 21 days (APPSC 2021, 2023). Under IDP 4.0 the portal processes 93+ clearances across 19 departments, still with a 21-day target (CDI).
The AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002 gives the single window statutory force, including deemed approval if a department misses its deadline .

Deemed approval in current practice: the City Gas Distribution policy (G.O. Ms. No. 8, Mar 2026) creates a single window, deemed clearances, a State Level Utilities Coordination Committee under the Chief Secretary, and committees headed by District Collectors (TH, 24 Mar 2026).

bullets: A higher saving and investment rate raises growth; a higher ICOR (less efficient capital) lowers it .

Capital formation may fail to raise output when capital is idle or badly used, or when complementary inputs are missing: skills, infrastructure, demand. Capital-intensive investment may also add little employment .

bullets: From 1 April 2022 MWCD schemes sit under three umbrella missions: Mission Shakti, Mission Vatsalya, Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 (APP; APPSC 2021 key "Three").

Samarthya (empowerment): Components Shakti Sadan (Swadhar Greh + Ujjawala merged), Sakhi Niwas (ex-Working Women Hostel), Palna (ex-National Creche Scheme), PMMVY, SANKALP-Hub for Empowerment of Women, Gap Funding for Economic Empowerment
Discontinued (exam trap): Mahila Shakti Kendra and Mahila Police Volunteers (CDI).
Stree Mano Raksha (Mar 2022): MWCD with NIMHANS, Bengaluru for women's mental health (APPSC 2021 key).
Exam angle: "Which is a sub-scheme of Mission Shakti?" Swadhar and Ujjawala no longer exist under their own names.

bullets: Deepam: Beneficiary Eligible households; Benefit 3 free LPG cylinders a year

Stree Shakti: Benefit design Free bus travel for women and transgender persons (AP domicile) in 5 APSRTC bus categories; later extended to PwD; Status / data Launched 15 Aug 2025; 71 crore+ free journeys (TH, 13 Jun 2026); women's share of bus travel 40% → 65%

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 3 Economy › C-5 › Social welfare programmes in AP - SC/ST/BC/minority welfare, pensions, housing, women and child welfare › Women and child welfare - Disha, ICDS, Kalyanamasthu/Shaadi Tohfa, Mahila Shakti
bullets: The AP Disha Bill, 2019 (after the Hyderabad case) promised a 7-day investigation, a 14-day trial and the death penalty. It never got assent, and the Cabinet withdrew it in Aug 2026 on the Centre's advice after the BNS and BNSS came in (TH, 7 Aug 2026).
ICDS: 55,746 Anganwadis and 257 projects. Mission Shakti runs One Stop Centres in all districts and the 181 helpline.

Stree Shakti (from 15 Aug 2025) gives free bus travel to women and transgender persons: 71 crore+ journeys (Jun 2026). The women's share of bus passengers rose from 40% to 65%. Divyang Shakti (Mar 2026) extends the benefit to persons with disabilities.

bullets: NTR Bharosa Pension (earlier YSR Pension Kanuka): ₹4,000/month to old-age and widow pensioners, enhanced from ₹3,000 w.e.f. April 2024 (APSES 2024-25).
Jan 2026: monthly distribution automated with Aadhaar-based biometric authentication to remove ghost beneficiaries; AP tops up the central NSAP pension from its own funds (APPCA).
2019-24: Name YSR Pension Kanuka (CDI quiz); Monthly amount (old age / widow) Raised in steps to ₹3,000 (APSES)

Scale: 61.92 lakh beneficiaries; ₹2,693 crore released for 1 Sep 2026; ₹73,506 crore spent on pensions since June 2024 (TH, 31 Aug 2026; earlier 63.12 lakh in Dec 2025, the largest share BC at 28.32 lakh). Budget 2026-27: ₹27,719 crore. The 16th Finance Commission found AP has the highest per-capita social security pension spending among States (CDI AP Budget).
Social security pensions - categories, amounts

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-6 › Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - social sector (health, education, nutrition, housing) › Code on Social Security 2020 - gig and platform workers, e-Shram, unorganised workers
bullets: It merges 9 laws (EPF, ESI, Maternity Benefit, Gratuity, Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act, etc.). The four Labour Codes came into force on 21 Nov 2025, with the 2026 Central Rules (CDI Block15).

It recognises gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in law for the first time. Aggregators pay 1-2% of annual turnover (capped at 5% of payouts) into a social security fund. A National Social Security Board recommends schemes (CDI; LENS Jul 2025). Maternity leave stays at 26 weeks; a creche is required at 50+ employees.

e-Shram (26 Aug 2021, MoLE): Aadhaar-verified National Database of Unorganised Workers; 12-digit UAN; age 16-59; excludes income-tax payers and EPFO/ESIC members. The 2024 One-Stop Solution joins up 15 schemes; 31.87 crore registered (LENSD, 26 Aug and 16 Aug 2026).

sections.topic: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 amendments to RTI
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Central Information Commission and State Information Commissions; CBI and its legal basis › Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 amendments to RTI
bullets: DPDP Act 2023 amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act to exempt personal information outright, removing the public-interest override . The Congress president said it "diluted the RTI Act's public interest clause" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

Economic Survey 2025-26 called for a "re-examination" of the RTI Act. It suggested exempting confidential service records and draft policy discussions, and floated a possible "ministerial veto" (TH, 31 Jan 2026).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-5 › Custodial violence, encounter deaths, prison reforms, death penalty debate › Mercy petitions - Arts 72 and 161, Shatrughan Chauhan
bullets: Art. 72 President: pardon incl. death sentence and court-martial .
Art. 161 Governor: cannot pardon a death sentence, but can commute/remit/suspend .
Shatrughan Chauhan v UOI (2014): inordinate, unexplained delay in deciding mercy petitions is a ground to commute death to life .
Also: solitary confinement before rejection is illegal; 14 days between rejection and execution .
Epuru Sudhakar v Govt of AP (2006): pardon/remission is open to limited judicial review .

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Election Commission of India - composition, appointment (2023 Act), powers and functions › CEC and Other ECs Act 2023 - selection committee, search committee, service conditions
bullets: Search Committee: Composition / rule Headed by the Law Minister + 2 Secretary-level members; shortlists 5 names

Selection Committee: Composition / rule PM (chair), Leader of Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) in the Lok Sabha, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM; may pick names outside the shortlist
The CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 (Act 49 of 2023) replaced the 1991 Act.

sections.topic: Transport in Andhra Pradesh · Railway tunnels and port rail links in AP
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-4 › Transport in Andhra Pradesh - highways, railway network, ports (Visakhapatnam, Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada), airports › Railway tunnels and port rail links in AP - longest electrified tunnel
bullets: Cherlopalli-Rapuru tunnel (6.6 km), SPSR Nellore - India's longest electrified rail tunnel when opened (2019), on the Obulavaripalle-Venkatachalam line that links Krishnapatnam port to the Rayalaseema hinterland . Nationally it is now exceeded by USBRL's T-50 (IYB).

Port rail links: Ramayapatnam sits next to NH-16 and Thettu station; Kakinada Gateway includes its own rail line (Survey 2025-26). Gap: last-mile rail to Kopparthy, Orvakal and Krishnapatnam nodes is incomplete (CDI Block10).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 4 Geography › D-4 › Patterns and issues in transport and trade - regional imbalance, connectivity gaps, logistics › Port-hinterland rail links - AP ports, Rayalaseema-coast links, tribal area roads
bullets: Rail links carry cement, granite and minerals to Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam. The last-mile rail links to industrial nodes such as Kopparthy and Orvakal are incomplete, so industry depends on road (CDI).
Guntakal-Ballari 3rd & 4th lines: Facts Rayalaseema to Karnataka and Goa, plus Krishnapatnam and Ramayapatnam ports; ₹1,264 crore, +16.22 MTPA, target 2028-29 (CCEA, Jul 2026)
Kottavalasa-Kirandul (KK): Facts Bailadila iron ore to Visakhapatnam port through Eastern Ghats tunnels
South Coast Railway, the 18th zone with its headquarters at Visakhapatnam, became operational on 1 Jun 2026 under the AP Reorganisation Act 2014.
Tribal roads (RCPLWE): 27 roads + 14 bridges (397 km) built in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Visakhapatnam and East Godavari (APSES).

Not in your sources: AP's VAT rates on petrol and diesel compared with Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

sections.topic: Sources of institutional finance for AP farmers

bullets: AP farmers borrow from commercial banks, RRBs and PACS, i.e. all of them (PYQ 2008). Other formal sources are SHGs/JLGs, microfinance and KCC.
Nationally, scheduled commercial banks give over 70% of formal farm credit. The cooperative system (PACS-DCCB-SCB) gives short-term credit, and ARDBs give long-term credit (LENS Apr 2026).
AP Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 review (Jan 2026): Rs 2.96 lakh crore disbursed to agriculture and allied sectors, Rs 1,490 crore to tenant farmers and Rs 95,714 crore to MSMEs (TH, 24 Jan 2026).
Formal credit excludes many tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers because it needs land records. A NABARD Guntur study found formal interest rates of about 2.5-10%.
KCC (1998, NABARD model scheme on the R.V. Gupta Committee): RBI's revised KCC Directions of 19 Jun 2026 apply to loans from 1 Jan 2027, with a maximum tenure of 6 years (earlier 5).

Size classes above are the standard Agriculture Census classes ; "small and marginal farmers" = holdings up to 2 ha.
Tenth Agriculture Census 2015-16 (still the standard all-India reference): 146 million operational holdings, average size 1.08 ha, down from 2.28 ha in 1971 - fragmentation (APPCA 2026).
Small and marginal farmers are about 86.2% of all farmers but hold only about 47% of the crop area (APPCA, May 2026).
Eleventh Agriculture Census 2021-22: provisional State results out; All-India 2021-22 figures are not yet the standard reference.

bullets: FRP is the legally mandated minimum price that sugar mills must pay cane farmers. It is set under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. The CCEA fixes it on CACP's recommendation and links it to the mill's sugar recovery % (LENSD, 8 May 2026).
FRP replaced the Statutory Minimum Price (SMP) from 2009-10 . State Advised Price (SAP) is a higher price that some States (e.g., UP, Punjab, Haryana) announce on top of FRP .

bullets: s.8B: Offence / provision Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Govt
Presumption of dowry death: BSA s.118 (Evidence Act 113B).
The Act penalises giving, taking or abetting dowry (IYB 2026).

Penalty for giving/taking: imprisonment of not less than 5 years and a fine of not less than ₹15,000 or the value of the dowry, whichever is more . CDX says "up to five years", but the Act sets five years as the minimum.
Offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable; the burden of proof lies on the accused; states appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers .

bullets: Meaning: rising share of women in the agricultural workforce (as cultivators, labourers and unpaid family workers) while men move to non-farm and urban work.

Causes: male out-migration to cities; distress - low household income pushes rural women into low-productivity farm work; concentration of women in subsistence farming and unpaid family work (LENSD, 24 Aug 2026); COVID-era return migration made women intensify farm work (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

Data: rural FLFPR (15+) rose 33.0% → 45.9% vs urban 23.3% → 27.7% (2019-20 to 2025); overall FLFPR 30% → 40%; rural women = 80% of the rise in female workers 2017-18 to 2023-24 (PLFS, LENSD 24 Aug 2026).
Women's WPR follows a U-shaped curve (Claudia Goldin): high in agriculture in the 1980s, fell with mechanisation 2004-05 to 2012, rising again after 2020 partly out of distress (TH, 25 Jul 2026).

Wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month (Cabinet, LENSD 17 Sep 2026). The ₹15,000 ceiling dated from Sep 2014; the change is expected to add 51 lakh+ employees. Benefits: PF, EPS pension, EDLI insurance.

ESI (ESI Act 1948): ceiling ₹21,000 a month; employer 3.25%, employee 0.75%; medical, sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits . Under the SS Code, ESIC coverage is pan-India (CDI); SPREE (Jul 2025-Jan 2026) added 1.03 crore employees (TH, 17 Jan 2026).

bullets: 1955: Event SBI Act: Imperial Bank became SBI, the first public sector bank; RBI bought 92% of its shares (APP)

1969 banks and their fate: Allahabad (now Indian Bank), BoB, BoI, BoM, Central, Canara, Dena (now BoB), Indian Bank, IOB, PNB, Syndicate (now Canara), UCO, Union, United Bank of India (now PNB) (APP).

Motives: social control of credit and a shift of credit to agriculture and small industry (APP; APPCA). The Lead Bank Scheme began the same year, 1969. The 50th anniversary was 19 July 2019.

Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, in force from 1 Aug 2025, made 19 amendments across the RBI Act, BR Act, SBI Act and the Banking Companies Acts of 1970 and 1980 (LENS Aug 2025).
"Substantial interest" threshold raised from ₹5 lakh to ₹2 crore; co-operative bank directors' tenure from 8 to 10 years; unclaimed PSB shares can go to the IEPF.

sections.topic: Party system in India · Consequences of coalition politics
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Party system in India - one-party dominance, multi-party and coalition eras › Consequences of coalition politics - stability, federalism, role of parties
bullets: Increased role of regional and small parties - the APPSC-keyed "major consequence".
Consensus building, but slow decisions; policy reversals/delays; compromises dilute strong measures (CDI).
Checks and balances: no single party holds absolute power; regional representation in national policy (CDI).
Defections and horse-trading led to the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule, 52nd Amendment, 1985) - the first time parties entered the Constitution.
Federalism became more bargained after 1989 (APP).

sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-3 › Indian political parties - evolution, ideology and classification › Party concepts - inner-party democracy, party system, social bases of parties, Kamaraj Plan
bullets: one-party dominance or the "Congress system" (1952-77);
India is a multi-party system because it divides along region, language, caste, religion and class.
Social bases: caste, region/language, religion and class. Regional parties rose on identity; for example, the TDP took power within 9 months on "Telugu atma gauravam".
Party problems listed: money power, criminalisation (Vohra Committee 1993), casteism, defections, weak ideology.
Kamaraj Plan (1963): senior Congress ministers resigned to work in the party organisation .

sections.topic: Caste in modern India · Caste and politics
sections.where: Prep notes · Book 2 Polity, Society & IR › B-4 › Caste in modern India - dominant caste, sanskritisation, caste associations, caste and politics › Caste and politics - vote banks, caste parties, politicisation of caste (Rajni Kothari)
bullets: Rajni Kothari edited *Caste in Indian Politics* (1970) ; his *Politics in India* links identities to electoral mobilisation (CDX).
The colonial roots run from the Minto-Morley Reforms 1909 (separate electorates) through vote-bank politics built on caste associations (APP).
Christophe Jaffrelot, *India's Silent Revolution*: the rise of lower castes through politics (CDX).
The conflict now is for power, not ritual status, and casteism in politics has increased (CDX).
Exam angle: RPSC 2013 A-R. Castes are being politicised, and casteism in politics is increasing. Both are true, but R is not the explanation.

sections.topic: Laws for women · Dowry Prohibition Act 1961

bullets: Dowry (s.2): property or valuable security given or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, before, at or any time after marriage in connection with it; excludes dower/mahr .
s.8B: Offence / provision Dowry Prohibition Officers appointed by the State Govt
Definition (Section 2): property or valuable security given, or agreed to be given, directly or indirectly, in connection with a marriage. Mahr under Muslim personal law is excluded .
Offences are cognisable, non-bailable and non-compoundable; the burden of proof lies on the accused; states appoint Dowry Prohibition Officers .
